title: 01 — System architecture and equipment
text: 01 — System architecture and equipment The homeowner reports that the system was first installed when the house was built in 1999 . The current Grundfos main-loop circulator carries production code PC 1240 (week 40 of 2012), identifying it as a later replacement. Its installation date is unknown. Heat source and hydraulics [USER] Two Polaris gas water heaters in series provide hot water for hydronic radiant heat and hydronic air-handler heating. Domestic hot water and space heating share the same water, per the homeowner. The right Polaris tank in the entrance photo supplies domestic hot water through a separate Caleffi thermostatic mixing valve above the tank. The homeowner reports a tank setting around 170 °F and a mixed domestic outlet around 105–110 °F. The homeowner confirmed from the SupplyHouse receipt that TMV-2 is a Caleffi 521 MixCal, SKU 521519AC, a 3/4-inch sweat three-way thermostatic mixing valve with temperature gauge and check valve. See the overhead mixer photo . [USER TRACE] The street cold-water branch feeds both the cold inlet of the domestic Caleffi mixer (TMV-2) and the left Polaris tank, at its lower side port labeled Cold Inlet. Left and right refer to the entrance view. [USER TRACE] Domestic hot water has a passive gravity recirculation loop. Both its supply and return connect to the right Polaris tank as seen from the entrance. The homeowner reports that it keeps hot water available in much of the house. The return descends between the tanks in the entrance photo, wraps around the right tank to its far side, and enters its lower side port labeled Cold Inlet. Copper from the top hot outlet of the right tank feeds the TMV-2 hot inlet. Street cold water enters the opposite port. The mixed outlet opposite the adjustment handle starts the domestic recirculation loop. [DOC] Homeowner water-heater note identifies model PG10 34-150-2NV , confirmed on both tank nameplates. Notes include condensate trap 186642-000 , O-ring AS568-327, 1.725-inch ID , stainless washer 2.187-inch diameter × .030-inch . These are parts research notes, not confirmed installed parts. [USER] Basement radiant is independent of DuoMix, with a dedicated on/off Taco 006-B4-11 circulator switched by a Honeywell R8222D1014 relay and Caleffi 521 thermostatic mixing valve. [USER/PHOTO] Two radiant mixed-temperature groups are controlled by a Wirsbo DuoMix 201 with separate Mix 1 and Mix 2 circulation outputs and Var 1/Var 2 injection pump outputs. [USER] Upstairs circulator Taco 008-BC6 ; researched replacement cartridge 008-045RP (compatibility still verify against nameplate). The homeowner identifies this pump as the Mix 2 mixed-water circulator. [USER] Two Lennox AM30 hydronic air handlers, one basement and one attic, provide supplemental forced air. The internal circulator nameplates for both AHU-1 and AHU-2 read Taco 006-B4-11 . Product-family PDF bundled; the basement AHU-1 cabinet is AM30Q2/3-70-2, serial 5898M07675. The attic AHU-2 cabinet is AM30Q2-40-2, serial 5801K48409. Detailed field wiring remains unverified. Controls cabinet [PHOTO] Two three-zone Wirsbo circuit boards on right side, one above the other; five visible external black relays: two above ZCM-1 and three above ZCM-2, mounted above respective boards; Wirsbo DuoMix 201 and other control board on left; dense multiconductor wiring. [USER] Trol-A-Temp MABS EZ-4 four-zone panel confirmed on cover. Zone assignments are mapped. Installed staging remains unverified. [PHOTO] Original proposed radiant piping drawing photographed; Garage Entry was proposed but [USER] not installed . Known versus inferred relationships [USER] Mix 1 corresponds to first-floor radiant; Mix 2 corresponds to upstairs radiant. [INFERENCE] A zone call must ultimately be converted to DuoMix demand and a switched circulator output; exact intervening components unknown. [OPEN] All valve locations, hydronic manifold layout, piping check valves, pump positions, sensor placement, boiler enable wiring, and safety interlocks. Equipment behind the Polaris tanks [USER/PHOTO] Basement radiant uses the lower-left Taco circulator and adjacent mechanical Caleffi mixing valve. [USER/PHOTO] The red Grundfos UPS 26-99 BFC (product 52722518) runs the main circulation loop upstairs and back. It corresponds to the pump shown above the tanks on the proposed drawing. Flow is left to right in the behind-tank photo. The homeowner reports that the loop rises to the attic AM30 (AHU-2) first, then continues to the Var 2 injection and Mix 2 radiant assembly, where the piping branches. MC-1 Boiler Enable switches pump hot from terminal 6 to terminal 5. A basement-only radiant call runs its own Taco. The basement-only call does not send a demand to MC-1, so that call does not start the Grundfos. [USER/PHOTO] The two higher light-brown Taco pumps are MC-1 Mix 1 on the left and Var 1 on the right, viewed from behind the tanks. [USER/PHOTO] The first-floor Honeywell valves run front to back in this view in the order Master Bath, Master Bedroom, then Main (Living Area). Two expansion tanks are visible below and to the right. Their circuit connections remain to be traced. [USER TRACE] At the right edge of the behind-tank basement photo, the near riser is the attic supply from the red Grundfos. The return riser is partly obscured directly behind it. It drops vertically, crosses the basement plumbing at the two expansion-tank connections, then continues to the Polaris return. The second-floor heating return enters the left Polaris tank at the port labeled “Heating System Inlet.” The heating circuit passes through the left tank first and then the right tank. See the behind-tank photo . Attic hydronic piping [USER/PHOTO] In the right-hand plumbing-wall view, the lowest horizontal run is the incoming main-loop supply from the basement. The AM30 coil branch comes off first and projects toward the camera. The main loop continues toward the Var 2 injection and Mix 2 radiant assembly, then returns downstairs. [USER/PHOTO] The brown Taco on the radiant supply is Mix 2. The Taco above the red and green valve handles on the right is Var 2. Mix 2 is a Taco 008-BC6 and flows right to left in this view. Var 2 flows upward. Its Taco nameplate appears to read 008-BC6 , pending confirmation because of glare. [USER/PHOTO] In the attic plumbing-wall photo, the Rest of Second Floor supply continues left through the left valve. The Yellow Room supply turns back to the right before passing through the right valve. The uppermost cross-frame pipe is the Rest of Second Floor manifold return, which tees into the Yellow Room return. The closely spaced supply and return elbows are separate pipes. [USER TRACE] Along the attic mixed-loop return toward the Mix 2 inlet, the Yellow Room and Rest of Second Floor manifold returns combine first. The connection back to the main branch is next, followed by the Var 2 discharge tee, then the Mix 2 inlet. Var 2 draws from the main supply from the basement downstream of the AHU-2 branch and injects upward into the pipe feeding Mix 2. [USER TRACE] Along the attic main loop from the basement, the AHU-2 coil supply tee comes first and the coil outlet rejoins the main a few inches downstream. Farther along the main loop, the Var 2 inlet and the Mix 2 circuit return connect through a second pair of closely spaced tees. [USER TRACE] In the attic plumbing-wall photo with the Honeywell MiniZone panel, the main-loop return is on the left and the supply is on the right. Both pass vertically through the framed wall’s bottom plate below the visible area. [USER/PHOTO] SUP 2 is located under the insulation immediately upstream of the Mix 2 inlet. The visible blue leads carry a tekmar 071 tag. See the sensor close-up . [USER/PHOTO] The high-point air eliminator beside the visible Honeywell valve is in service. The switch labeled “Furnace” powers AHU-2, a Lennox AM30 hydronic air handler. See the right-hand attic photo . The Yellow Room radiant manifold is at the far end of the attic mechanical room beside Var 2. In the manifold photo, the right header with the small valves supplies the floor loops and the left header collects their return. The Rest of Second Floor radiant manifold has its supply on the lower, farther header with the small valves. The upper, nearer header collects the return. Polaris heating supply branches [USER TRACE] The upper side port labeled Heating System Outlet on the right Polaris tank (entrance view) feeds the heating supply header. In order from the tank, the first tee feeds the basement radiant loop, the second tee feeds the red Grundfos, and the elbow beyond both tees feeds the basement Lennox AM30 (AHU-1). The basement radiant branch has its own Taco circulator and Caleffi mixer. See the outlet branch photo . [USER TRACE] The basement radiant manifold return comes around the corner toward the expansion tanks, rises, and tees into the common heating return just beyond the expansion-tank connections, toward the left Polaris Heating System Inlet. The nearby tees serve separate connections. Their spacing does not indicate a paired supply and return connection for the basement radiant circuit. [USER/PHOTO] A temperature probe is mounted on the common heating return downstream of the basement radiant return tee, left of the expansion tanks. Its blue leads are visible behind the Grundfos. See the return probe photo . [USER TRACE] The basement AM30 (AHU-1) coil return joins the same common heating return near the left Polaris Heating System Inlet. The green-handled valve in the heating outlet branch photo identifies the AM30 return line. [USER TRACE] The insulated intertank pipe runs from the left Polaris upper Heating System Outlet to the right Polaris lower Heating System Inlet . Left and right refer to the entrance view. The second-floor heating return enters the left tank, passes through both tanks in series, and leaves the right tank through its Heating System Outlet. See the intertank pipe photo . First-floor radiant injection piping [USER TRACE] Var 1 (right pump, Taco 008-BC6 ) draws from the main loop as it returns from upstairs. That branch feeds the Mix 1 circuit, which rejoins the same main return through the other of two closely spaced tees at the right of the photo. Mix 1 is the left pump, a Taco 006-B4-11 . Both pumps flow right to left in this view. The blue sensor lead is visible immediately upstream of Mix 1. The blue sensor leads splice to red and white conductors in a brown-jacketed thermostat cable. A red conductor lands on MC-1 SUP 1, making this the likely SUP 1 sensor. The cable disappears into a bundle before the controller, so end-to-end identity and the white conductor termination remain unverified. See the Mix 1 and Var 1 close-up . [USER TRACE] Mix 1 discharge splits into three branches for Master Bath, Master Bedroom, and Main (Living Area). Each branch passes through its Honeywell zone valve before reaching its supply manifold. Elbows turn the flow left to right through the valves toward the manifolds in the overhead view. See the overhead photo . [USER TRACE] The Master Bath, Master Bedroom, and Main (Living Area) returns collect in one common first-floor return manifold visible just below Mix 1 in the Mix 1 and Var 1 close-up. From that manifold toward Mix 1, the lower pipe below Var 1 connects back to the main return first. Farther along, Var 1 discharges into the pipe feeding the Mix 1 inlet. Var 1 draws from the main loop returning from upstairs. Basement radiant mixer and manifold [USER/PHOTO] The hot supply from the right Polaris heating header enters the Caleffi mixer from above. The basement Taco circulator is in the foreground and the manifold is behind it. At the right behind the wiring, the front and rear pipes visually overlap and remain separate at that point. The Caleffi mixed outlet runs left through the branch with the red-handled valve to the Taco inlet. The bottom port runs down and across to the basement radiant return manifold. The manifold return continues downstream to its tee into the common heating return by the expansion tanks. The Taco discharge feeds the basement radiant supply manifold directly. The homeowner traced the street cold-water feed to the Polaris and domestic mixer branch and saw no identifiable pressure-reducing valve along the route. Presence elsewhere remains unverified. title: 05 — Active fault: second-floor radiant circulator
text: 05 — Active fault: second-floor radiant circulator Diagnostic rule: Voltage across connected TELESTAT R1/R2 is a clue about the feedback circuit. It cannot establish end-switch closure or determine whether the ZCM is faulty. Both upstairs inputs dropped to 0 VAC on a call even though their isolated valve end switches read OL. Verify closure independently, then assess the module by its ES output and the corresponding DuoMix demand response with verified feedback applied. Current diagnosis: Both upstairs valves moved on a call but their isolated end switches stayed OL. The working Living Room switch showed continuity during demand. Inspect valve travel and switch actuation first. ZCM-2 replacement is deferred until its response to valid feedback can be checked. Symptom [USER] Rest of Second Floor thermostat calls for heat; the corresponding ZCM-2 radiant zone control module yellow indicator illuminates, but DuoMix LCD shows no visible response and Mix 2 mixed-water circulator does not receive 120 V at DuoMix terminal 8 under test conditions. By contrast, a first-floor call produces 120 V at Mix 1 mixed-water circulator terminal 12 . Do not extrapolate voltage readings to other conditions; the meter reference, time since call, and settings were not logged. What is actually established Thermostat call correlates with lower radiant zone control module zone-1 yellow indicator. At least some electrical path reaches or affects the radiant zone control module; LED meaning not independently verified. Mix 2 mixed-water circulator switched-hot output was not active when checked; this does not by itself prove DuoMix fault. Mix 1 output is capable of energizing during a different zone call. No visible LCD change was reported; display interpretation remains unverified. The Yellow Room's 17/20 conductors are supply sensor, not Mix 2 demand . Fault tree (unverified branches) Missing demand at DuoMix 3–4: board OUTPUT issue, upstream external relay/contact, Honeywell valve end switch (if used), loose wire, staging control. Demand reaches DuoMix but output inhibited: control logic, sensor/outdoor conditions, settings, pump protection, internal relay failure. Apparent failure due to test conditions: time delay, sensor state, incomplete thermostat call, wrong meter reference, wrong assumed output. Test plan (visual/non-invasive first) Photograph DuoMix 3–4 and follow each conductor physically to source. Record cable IDs and terminal labels. Photograph external relay part numbers and all terminals; trace contacts versus coils with power safely isolated and qualified assistance. Identify Honeywell valve model and observe mechanical position during sustained call; trace any end-switch wires. Document the right-side OUTPUT labels and wires on ZCM-2 (installed part A303XX0003 ). Locate manufacturer's instructions before electrical testing. Record all indicators and DuoMix display during controlled, sustained upstairs demand; note elapsed minutes and room/pipe temperatures. If professionally tested, compare actual state of DuoMix 3–4 with active call to determine upstream versus controller-side fault; never short terminals or inject voltage without confirmed manufacturer instructions. Prior service clue [USER] Replacement Wirsbo zone-controller box contained handwritten note “no output on zone 3.” Board/date/author and meaning of output unknown. Current problem is lower radiant zone control module zone 1 , so the note is context, not diagnosis. Whether a removed board is in box was asked but not answered. 2026-11-07: simultaneous upstairs zone demand (new photographs) [USER] Both upstairs zones (Rest of Second Floor and Bedroom Above Garage) calling at once. [OBSERVED PHOTO] ZCM-2 radiant zone control module has two illuminated amber LEDs adjacent to printed TELESTAT legends, one for each active zone; green 24V LED illuminated. [OBSERVED PHOTO] DuoMix 201 LCD reads OPEN with upper item text not confidently transcribed. User reports neither upstairs call appears as a Mix 2 demand on DuoMix. This does not prove whether terminals 3–4 are open, or what OPEN refers to; it may be a selected diagnostic/menu value rather than a global demand status. Do not assume amber LEDs prove valve position or contact closure. Photos: ../photos/IMG_81CD45AE-2742-4ED7-989A-802AA7705E40.jpeg (DuoMix) and ../photos/IMG_3FA9E00D-211B-43EB-838B-A3E298D1D1E3.jpeg (Wirsbo). Next discriminator: identify wires and verified electrical state of DuoMix Mix 2 Demand 3–4 under simultaneous call; separately determine what display item shows OPEN. 2026-11-07 — Major diagnostic breakthrough: comparative ES voltage Using a multimeter set to V~ (AC) , the homeowner measured directly across the two ES terminals on each radiant zone control module: Controller Condition Across ES/ES Upper (working Mix 1) No first-floor call 27.2 VAC Upper (working Mix 1) One first-floor zone calling ~1 VAC Lower (suspect Mix 2) Both upstairs zones calling 27.2 VAC Lower (suspect Mix 2) Both upstairs zones satisfied 27.2 VAC Voltage interpretation: These are AC voltage readings across the two ES terminals with the circuit connected. ZCM-1 dropping from 27.2 VAC to about 1 VAC is consistent with its contact closing. ZCM-2 retaining 27.2 VAC during the call shows the terminals did not come to nearly the same potential. In the traced demand circuit, that is consistent with an open or high-resistance ES path. The reading alone cannot distinguish a relay that was never commanded from a failed contact or a wiring fault, or establish what MC-1 sees across terminals 3 and 4. Unverified causes: Missing actuator travel or end-switch feedback, an external interlock or wiring fault, or a fault in the ZCM-2 ES relay or associated circuitry. The installed A303XX0003 activation sequence remains unverified. Traced wiring: Upper ES brown -> DuoMix 1; lower ES upper red -> DuoMix 3; lower ES lower white -> upper radiant zone control module -> apparent 24 VAC transformer; DuoMix 2 and 4 tied together. ES terminals are not the separate OUTPUT terminals. [USER] Yellow Room call: The initial closed-valve observation was made after the call had stopped. On recheck during the same call, yellow remained lit, lower red stayed off, and the valve still felt open. The observation does not distinguish contact closure from any coincident change in the board’s sensing voltage. Basement radiant uses one dedicated Taco and a mechanical mixer; Honeywell R8222D1014 switches its 120 V supply. No basement radiant ZCM, MC-1 demand, or basement-only Grundfos start is reported. Shared white transformer wiring to brown and upper black relays appears to be 24 VAC common, not a demonstrated 120 V neutral. Checked ZCM upper THERMOSTAT 2 → relay lug 2 red; THERMOSTAT 3 → relay lug 4 white; SB and 4 unused. Complete relay roles remain unresolved. MC-1 Boiler Enable: terminal 6 receives 120 V hot; terminal 5 supplies Grundfos hot; pump white returns to supply neutral. It is not traced to Polaris burner enable. Domestic water is shared with heating. Street cold feeds left Polaris Cold Inlet and TMV-2 cold inlet. Right top domestic hot outlet feeds TMV-2 hot inlet; mixed outlet feeds distribution/passive recirculation; return enters right Cold Inlet. Domestic mixer is receipt-confirmed Caleffi 521519AC. Basement mixer is Caleffi 521, exact suffix unverified. Basement AM30 model AM30Q2/3-70-2, serial 5898M07675. Attic AM30Q2-40-2, serial 5801K48409. Both internal pumps are Taco 006-B4-11; so are Mix 1 and basement radiant. Mix 2 and Var 1 are 008-BC6; Var 2 appears 008-BC6, provisional due to glare. MABS EZ-4 downstairs: Zone 1 Living Area, Zone 2 Master Bedroom, Zone 3 Basement. EMM-3 attic: Zone 1 Rest of Second Floor, Zone 2 Yellow Room. Equipment-to-AM30 cable identities and staging are inferred, not traced end to end. Stage 2 retaining stage 1 is a homeowner expectation. With failed upstairs end-switch feedback, stage 1 demand alone does not prove Grundfos operation. Independent air-only main-loop enable remains open. Grundfos PC 1240 is a production date code, not a proven installation date. System original installation is homeowner-reported 1999. Right tank reported ~170 °F and domestic mixed outlet ~105–110 °F are observations, not recommended settings. Both Polaris plates mark 160 °F outlet operation. AM30 maximum inlet is 180 °F. Pressure-reducing valve was not identified along the traced cold feed; absence elsewhere is not proven. Gauge ~65 psi is one uncalibrated snapshot. The 450 psi C26 rating concerns refrigerant.
